reason: 'Can't see my latest bank transfer' does not say whether the transfer is incoming (balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer) or outgoing (pending_transfer); gold is defensible but not determined by the text.
Asking how long a refund takes is the dataset's standard phrasing for waiting on a refund that hasn't appeared; request_refund is about initiating one.
Topping up from an Apple Watch is an Apple Pay question; gold fits.
'Who else can top up my account' is generic: it could be third-party card top-ups (gold) or receiving_money from friends; nothing in the text mentions a card.

'I transferred some money' reads most naturally as an outgoing transfer (transfer_not_received_by_recipient/pending_transfer), but a top-up by bank transfer that never landed is also possible, so gold is defensible but unproven.

'I need my PIN' never mentions a card; the dataset routes PIN-retrieval to get_physical_card (its FAQ covers the card PIN), so gold is a convention rather than something a literal reader would pick, and change_pin is equally plausible.
Asking why there are fees for card usage matches card_payment_fee_charged.
A question about fees on transfers is transfer_fee_charged.
'How much am I charged to receive money' could mean fees on incoming bank transfers (gold) or the general receiving_money intent; the text does not specify a method.
User asks about the pattern of fees on card payments; gold fits.
A top-up that was cancelled/reverted is top_up_reverted, not top_up_failed.
Explicit Google Pay top-up question; gold fits.
Top-up cancelled after the fact is top_up_reverted.
Asking whether a top-up was cancelled is top_up_reverted.
Apple Pay eligibility for top-up is the apple_pay_or_google_pay intent.
The message never mentions a cash withdrawal (or a card payment); nothing supports the withdrawal-specific intent, so a generic exchange_rate query is the only label the text licenses.
How to top up with Apple Pay is exactly apple_pay_or_google_pay.
'Where can I receive my card' could be a delivery-address question during ordering (gold), a delivery-estimate question, or a country_support question; the text underdetermines it.
'My money transfer has not arrived' is the canonical transfer_not_received_by_recipient phrasing; incoming-transfer reading is possible but gold is fine.
User already requested a refund from the seller a week ago and it hasn't appeared; that is Refund_not_showing_up.
Literally a request for a new card (order_physical_card); the US-residence clause makes country_support defensible, but the user is not asking whether the country is supported.
Enabling contactless in security settings is the contactless_not_working intent.
'Payment not gone through' could equally mean declined_card_payment or pending_card_payment; the text does not distinguish.

A 'transaction taking a very long time' is most naturally pending_transfer (or pending_card_payment); transfer_not_received_by_recipient is defensible but the text never says a recipient is missing funds.
Asking how long ID verification takes is a process question (verify_my_identity); unable_to_verify_identity assumes a failure the text does not state.
Asking whether contactless is enabled on a new card is the contactless_not_working intent.
'Can friends add to my account' is generic; receiving_money and topping_up_by_card are both defensible and no card is mentioned.
Unable to withdraw funds is declined_cash_withdrawal.
'Where is my deposit' is the cheque/cash deposit intent; 'deposit' is the distinguishing word.
'Where is the virtual card' is getting_virtual_card.
